title: Tradition and the Heart

questions.question: Why did the Pharisees confront Jesus regarding some of His disciples eating?
options: They noticed they were eating with defiled hands, that is, unwashed
They noticed they were eating pork
They were eating food offered to idols
They were overindulging in wine
questions.correctAnswer: They noticed they were eating with defiled hands, that is, unwashed
questions.explanation: Mark 7:2 (ESV): "They saw that some of his disciples ate with hands that were defiled, that is, unwashed."

questions.question: The Pharisees and all the Jews do not eat unless they wash their hands properly, holding to the tradition of whom?
options: The elders
The high priests
Prophet Samuel
King Solomon
questions.explanation: Mark 7:3 (ESV): "(For the Pharisees and all the Jews do not eat unless they wash their hands properly, holding to the tradition of the elders,)"

questions.question: Jesus calls them hypocrites, quoting Isaiah: "This people honors me with their lips, but their... ?"
options: "their heart is far from me;"
"their minds are devoid of truth;"
"their actions reflect the devil;"
"their temple is full of lies;"
questions.explanation: Mark 7:6 (ESV): "...as it is written, 'This people honors me with their lips, but their heart is far from me;'"

questions.question: Jesus accused the Pharisees of saying that whoever tells their parents, "Whatever you would have gained from me is Corban." What does "Corban" mean?
options: Given to God
Cursed by God
Tithed prematurely
Stored for the Sabbath
questions.explanation: Mark 7:11 (ESV): "But you say, 'If a man tells his father or his mother, "Whatever you would have gained from me is Corban"' (that is, given to God)—"

questions.question: By allowing Corban in this way, Jesus said they were making void the word of God in order to do what?
options: Hold to their tradition that they had handed down
Keep all the money for themselves
Defy the Romans secretly
Avoid caring for the poor
questions.correctAnswer: Hold to their tradition that they had handed down
questions.explanation: Mark 7:13 (ESV): "thus making void the word of God by your tradition that you have handed down. And many such things you do."

questions.question: What did Jesus say defiles a person?
options: The things that come out of a person
The food that goes into a person's mouth
Walking through a Gentile marketplace
Touching the sick without washing
questions.correctAnswer: The things that come out of a person
questions.explanation: Mark 7:15 (ESV): "There is nothing outside a person that by going into him can defile him, but the things that come out of a person are what defile him."

questions.question: By explaining that whatever goes into a person from outside cannot defile him, Mark adds a parenthetical note that Jesus was doing what?
options: Thus he declared all foods clean
Thus he destroyed the law of Moses entirely
Thus he ended all temple sacrifices
Thus he angered the high council more
questions.correctAnswer: Thus he declared all foods clean
questions.explanation: Mark 7:19 (ESV): "since it enters not his heart but his stomach, and is expelled?" (Thus he declared all foods clean.)"

questions.question: Where do the evil intentions that defile a person (like sexual immorality, theft, murder, deceit) come from?
options: From within, out of the heart of man
From the spiritual forces in heavenly places
From the teachings of wicked men
From eating unclean foods over time
questions.correctAnswer: From within, out of the heart of man
questions.explanation: Mark 7:21 (ESV): "For from within, out of the heart of man, come evil thoughts, sexual immorality, theft, murder, adultery..."

questions.question: When Jesus went to the region of Tyre and Sidon, who came falling at His feet?
options: A Syrophoenician woman whose little daughter had an unclean spirit
A Roman centurion whose servant was dying
A blind man calling Him "Son of David"
A leper living outside the city walls
questions.correctAnswer: A Syrophoenician woman whose little daughter had an unclean spirit
questions.explanation: Mark 7:25-26 (ESV): "But immediately a woman whose little daughter had an unclean spirit heard of him and came and fell down at his feet. Now the woman was a Gentile, a Syrophoenician by birth."

questions.question: How did the Syrophoenician woman reply when Jesus said, "Let the children be fed first, for it is not right to take the children's bread and throw it to the dogs"?
options: "Yes, Lord; yet even the dogs under the table eat the children's crumbs."
"I am no dog, for I believe in the God of Israel."
"Then I will go unfed, but spare my daughter."
"Are not all men children to the Lord?"
questions.correctAnswer: "Yes, Lord; yet even the dogs under the table eat the children's crumbs."
questions.explanation: Mark 7:28 (ESV): "But she answered him, 'Yes, Lord; yet even the dogs under the table eat the children's crumbs.'"

questions.question: Why did Jesus grant the Syrophoenician woman's request to cast the demon out of her daughter?
options: "For this statement you may go your way; the demon has left your daughter."
"Because you are destitute, I will have mercy."
"Because of your many tears."
"To show the Pharisees that faith is greater than birth."
questions.correctAnswer: "For this statement you may go your way; the demon has left your daughter."
questions.explanation: Mark 7:29 (ESV): "And he said to her, 'For this statement you may go your way; the demon has left your daughter.'"

questions.question: When they brought to Jesus a man who was deaf and had a speech impediment, what did Jesus do before saying "Ephphatha"?
options: He put his fingers into his ears, and after spitting touched his tongue
He washed the man's face in a nearby stream
He poured oil on his head and commanded the spirit to leave
He rubbed mud on his ears and mouth
questions.correctAnswer: He put his fingers into his ears, and after spitting touched his tongue
questions.explanation: Mark 7:33 (ESV): "And taking him aside from the crowd privately, he put his fingers into his ears, and after spitting touched his tongue."

questions.question: Looking up to heaven, Jesus sighed and said "Ephphatha." What does this mean?
options: "Be opened."
"Hear and speak."
"Be healed."
"Depart from him."
questions.explanation: Mark 7:34 (ESV): "...he sighed and said to him, 'Ephphatha,' that is, 'Be opened.'"

questions.question: What did Jesus charge the people to do after He healed the deaf man?
options: He charged them to tell no one
He charged them to tell the synagogue ruler
He charged them to sacrifice a lamb
He charged them to follow Him into the desert
questions.correctAnswer: He charged them to tell no one
questions.explanation: Mark 7:36 (ESV): "And Jesus charged them to tell no one. But the more he charged them, the more zealously they proclaimed it."

questions.question: The people were astonished beyond measure, saying, "He has done all things well. He even makes ___?"
options: "the deaf hear and the mute speak."
"the lame to dance and the blind to see clearly."
"the stormy sea calm and demons flee in fear."
"the unlearned speak the deepest truths of God."
questions.correctAnswer: "the deaf hear and the mute speak."
questions.explanation: Mark 7:37 (ESV): "And they were astonished beyond measure, saying, 'He has done all things well. He even makes the deaf hear and the mute speak.'"

key_verse_text: "There is nothing outside a person that by going into him can defile him, but the things that come out of a person are what defile him."
